comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose their exposure to foreign exchange risks arising from non-U.S. subsidiaries. Citi specifically identifies its Argentine operations as a net investment exposed to currency fluctuation, whereas Bank of America broadly categorizes 'investments in non-U.S. subsidiaries' as instruments exposed to this risk. Citi details the specific accounting treatment (remeasuring net ARS assets using the official rate into earnings), while Bank of America lists the asset types but does not provide specific quantitative exposure or accounting impacts for Argentina in this segment.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024, Citi's net investment in its Argentine operations was approximately $1.5 billion (compared to $1.3 billion at September 30, 2024).
Citi uses Argentina's official market exchange rate to remeasure its net ARS-denominated assets into USD.

The types of instruments exposed to this risk include investments in non-U.S. subsidiaries, foreign currency-denominated loans and securities, future cash flows in foreign currencies arising from foreign exchange transactions, foreign currency-denominated debt and various foreign exchange derivatives whose values fluctuate with changes in the level or volatility of currency exchange rates or non-U.S. interest rates.
